title: Computational Genomics & Rare Disease Mapping
school: Yale Graduate School of Arts and Sciences

sections.abstract: Julian Thorne proposes scalable graph neural network architectures for identifying non-coding genomic mutations in pediatric rare diseases.
sections.scientific_methodology: Graph transformer pipeline trained on 15,000 whole-genome sequences from the Yale Center for Genome Analysis. Validates variant pathogenicity with high specificity.
sections.impact_and_dissemination: Open-access bioinformatics pipelines and diagnostic models shared with clinical geneticists across the Yale-New Haven Health System.
sections.work_packages: Milestone 1: Sequence pre-processing. Milestone 2: Model fine-tuning. Milestone 3: Clinical concordance study.
sections.budget: Includes $4,200 requested for an ultra-high-end liquid-cooled personal workstation, exceeding standard $2,500 institutional tech allowance.

video_transcript: Good morning committee. I am Julian Thorne. My research focuses on rare pediatric genomics at Yale Medical School. I am requesting emergency tech funds for deep learning hardware.
